title: XBOW researchers used AI agents to win a $250,000 Chrome exploit bounty
source_used: XBOW's own blog post of 13 Oct 2026 (full text) and Startup Fortune (full text, the pool source)
key_facts: XBOW, an autonomous-security start-up, says it built a Chrome "full-chain" exploit (three linked bugs that together take over a Windows computer from a web page) and won a $250,000 bounty from Google, the first under Google's 2026 rules.
Four XBOW researchers worked with OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol, a publicly available model, and say the compute for the awarded chain cost $40,000.
After Google said it already knew one bug in the first chain, the team built a new chain between Sunday 2 Aug and Friday 7 Aug 2026.
The AI searched Chrome's source code, tested ideas, built proofs of concept and wrote early exploit drafts; humans set strategy, chose where to look and checked the agents' work.
XBOW says all three bugs are fixed and tells users to keep Chrome current and relaunch it when the Update button appears.
Startup Fortune reports Google reproduced and confirmed the bugs, shipped fixes, and that none was exploited against real users, all according to XBOW.
XBOW estimates the chain affected "a billion users" and says similar work once took teams months; it believes agents alone could find each of the three bugs within a year.
quote_evidence: The compute we used over six days for the awarded chain cost $40,000, a fraction of the bounty.
The AI searched Chrome's source code, tested ideas, built proofs of concept, and wrote the earliest drafts of the exploit.
Earlier this year, it won our company a $250,000 bounty from Google, the first under its 2026 new rules.
why_it_matters_hint: AI agents working with human researchers cut the time to find a serious Chrome attack chain from months to days, which helps defenders and attackers alike.
event_date: Exploit built 2-7 Aug 2026; bounty 'earlier this year'; details first published 13 Oct 2026
notes: All figures (cost, timeline, billion users, Google's payment) are XBOW's own claims; no Google statement was read. The work dates from August but the public disclosure is 13 Oct 2026, so treated as new.
